items.title: RENN Asia Wellness offers free health checks worth RM500,000
items.summary: As part of the government's Hari Kebangsaan Hari Malaysia campaign, RENN Asia Wellness said the health checks comprise the AtCor Arterial Stiffness Test, Quantum Vitamin & Mineral Analysis and MicroCirculation Analysis. RENN Asia Wellness founder and chief executive officer Jonathan Chew said preventive health should become part of routine health management rather than something considered only when a person feels unwell. [[nid:1532731]] The AtCor test evaluates central blood pressure and arterial stiffness, while the Quantum Vitamin & Mineral Analysis assesses vitamin and mineral status and the MicroCirculation Analysis examines blood circulation through the body's smallest blood vessels.

items.title: PDZ Holdings proposes RM65.4mil capital reduction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PDZ Holdings Bhd (PDZ) has proposed a capital reduction exercise to cancel RM65.4 million of its issued share capital to set off against the company's accumulated losses. As of August 17, PDZ's issued share capital stands at RM158.57 million, comprising 588.37 million ordinary shares. Following the capital reduction, the issued share capital will be reduced to RM93.17 million, while maintaining the exact same total number of shares in issue.

items.title: Petronas secured 5-year LNG supply agreement to Greece
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) unit Petco Trading (UK) Ltd, has secured a five-year agreement to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Greece, strengthening its presence in Europe and the wider Southeast European energy market. Petronas executive vice-president and chief executive officer of Gas & Maritime Business Datuk Adif Zulkifli said the agreement demonstrated the company's commitment to providing reliable and flexible LNG solutions as markets navigate energy security, affordability and energy transition priorities. "This agreement with Metlen underscores Petronas' commitment to delivering reliable and flexible LNG solutions that support our customers' evolving energy needs.

items.title: Carried by teenager porter, rescued Croatian climber says Kinabalu ordeal broke his heart
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed regret over the risks he took after being found injured and alone on Mount Kinabalu for eight days, but said the ordeal strengthened his faith in human compassion. Persic, 46, said the rescue operation was a humbling experience, particularly when rescuers and porters had to carry him down because he was too weak and injured to continue on his own, Berita Harian reported. 40 people risking their lives to save one.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Second multi-purpose mission ship under construction in Turkiye to be completed by end‑2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The second Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS), which is currently under construction in Turkiye, is expected to be completed and handed over to the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the first MPMS vessel was expected to arrive in March next year, a month before the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA). Saifuddin Nasution said he would travel to Istanbul, Turkiye, at the end of this month to personally inspect the progress of the vessel’s construction.

items.title: Nepal tragedy: Families question search for 55 Malaysians
items.summary: Families in Hope spokesman Dr R. Manivannan, who represents 49 of the 55 affected families, said their concern was not about the dedication, professionalism or courage of SMART personnel, but the timing, strategy, prioritisation and what was actually achieved. But after 20 days, families are entitled to ask difficult questions, " he said. He said families had provided photographs, videos, timestamps, communications, travel movements, GPS-related evidence, eyewitness information, travel-group movements and immigration and checkpoint information.

items.title: Negri Sembilan DKU declares April proclamation invalid
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared that the proclamation dated April 19, 2026, relating to the abdication of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is unconstitutional and invalid. Secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said three of the four individuals who signed the proclamation did not hold the position of Undang under the adat of their respective luak on the date in question. "Therefore, the proclamation dated April 19, 2026, was flawed from the outset," he said in a statement here following decisions reached at a special DKU meeting held in Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, yesterday.

items.title: Four Chinese citizens to be charged over Kedah kidnapping
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Three men and a woman, all Chinese citizens, will be charged at the Alor Setar court tomorrow in connection with the kidnapping of a woman at a house in Taman Amira, Jalan Langgar, last month. Six people were arrested, comprising a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged in their 20s to 40s. On Sept 10, one of the suspects was charged at the Alor Setar Sessions Court with kidnapping a woman from China last month.

items.title: Indonesia's president sacks finance minister, promotes deputy
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has sacked finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa and appointed his deputy Suahasil Nazara as his replacement, the president's office said on Monday. Suahasil Nazara, deputy finance minister since 2019, was among senior officials who arrived at the state palace for a swearing-in ceremony, while Purbaya, 61, was earlier seen leaving during a parliamentary hearing. The straight-talking Purbaya had replaced long-standing finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati in September last year as Prabowo sought aggressive pro-growth policies over fiscal prudence.

items.title: Anthony Loke calls for Pakatan Presidential Council meeting to discuss recent political developments after Umno assembly
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will propose to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council convene to discuss recent political developments following statements made at the Umno General Assembly. He said the recent statements raised concerns regarding political certainty and stability, which could affect investor and public confidence in the country. The Prime Minister must also make this clear with all component parties,” the Transport Minister said.

items.title: Pacific Partnership 2026 shows strength of multinational cooperation, says US Admiral
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Differences in language, culture, and organisational structures did not prevent countries from working effectively together during Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26), said US Pacific Fleet commander Admiral Stephen Thomas Koehler. He said the two-week Malaysia leg demonstrated how nations could overcome those differences while working towards a common mission of strengthening disaster preparedness and response. "What we accomplished here proves that in the Pacific, the ocean is not what separates us — it's what brings us together," he said during the Malaysia Pacific Partnership closing ceremony at INTAN Sabah today.

items.title: Federal Court reserves decision on PKR's RM10 mil bond appeal against Zuraida
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court today reserved its decision on PKR's appeal to reinstate a High Court ruling ordering former Ampang member of parliament Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million for breaching a party bond. PKR counsel Ranjit Singh submitted that Zuraida had contractually admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the bond's operative clause fixed that exact sum upon default. "Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events," Ranjit said during the appeal against a Court of Appeal decision that reduced the quantum to RM100,000.

items.title: Malaysian woman nabbed with 8kg of cannabis at Hong Kong airport
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 33-year-old Malaysian woman was arrested in Hong Kong after she was allegedly caught attempting to smuggle about eight kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds worth HK$1.6 million (RM830,000) into the territory on Saturday. Hong Kong Customs said the woman had arrived at Hong Kong International Airport from Bangkok, Thailand, before she was detained during a customs inspection. Hong Kong Customs said it would continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking through intelligence-led analysis.

items.title: Penang Port Commission, PPSB to offer free ferry services on Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) are offering free ferry services to Malaysians on September 16 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations and the Keretapi Sarong Festival. SPPP chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the offer applies to trips from both ferry terminals, Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Seberang Perai and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) here, in accordance with the existing service schedule. According to him, during last year’s Malaysia Day celebration, a total of 10,094 pedestrians and 1,909 two-wheeled vehicles utilised the ferry service for round trips.

items.title: Rohingya family living rough outside Bandar Baru Uda offices for a week
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A Rohingya family, including a pregnant woman and an infant, has been living rough on a pavement outside office buildings in Bandar Baru Uda here for about a week. The family, comprising the woman and her children, has been sleeping on a carpet spread along the walkway at Jalan Padi 1. Business operators in the area said the family's presence had caused inconvenience to people visiting nearby offices. The family's presence also went viral today after a post in the Pasal Johor Facebook group drew public attention to them.

items.title: Negri Sembilan MB tight-lipped on royal proclamation issue, Zahid meeting
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim remained tight-lipped over an alleged proclamation seeking the removal of state ruler Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Ismail also declined to comment on the outcome of his meeting with Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and three party vice-presidents on Thursday. The meeting followed Zahid's earlier statement seeking clarification from Ismai l regarding claims that the menteri besar was forced to sign a proclamation document to depose Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on Aug 3.

items.title: Chief of Defence Force: MAF proposes reinstating multi‑agency border‑security framework used under former national task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) has submitted a proposal to the National Security Council (NSC) to reinstate a multi-agency operational framework modelled on the National Task Force (NTF) to bolster national border security. Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the proposal, submitted through the National Operational Management Committee, would bring together various agencies including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), and the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM). He said the strategic coordination of enforcement agencies has proven more effective in addressing security vulnerabilities along the country’s land and maritime borders.

items.title: Two‑year‑old mauled by stray dogs in Batu Pahat to undergo reconstructive surgery
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 14 — A two-year-old girl mauled by stray dogs outside her grandmother’s home in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, is expected to undergo reconstructive surgery soon as she continues to fight for her life. Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi was critically injured in the Sept 6 attack by five dogs, suffering severe head and facial wounds. Previously, the authorities caught seven dogs, including five puppies, which attacked Haira.

items.title: Don't take law into own hands over Rohingya issue, cops warn
items.summary: BACHOK: Police have warned the public, including social media influencers, against taking matters into their own hands over issues involving the Rohingya community and its settlements. Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said such matters should be left to the authorities, including the police and Immigration Department. Also present were Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and UMK vice-chancellor Datuk Prof Dr Arham Abdullah.

items.title: Govt opens door to more vehicle inspection centres: Anthony Loke
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: The government wants to see more MV15 vehicle inspection centres opened nationwide to improve access for vehicle owners, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the government will not limit the number of operators for MV15 inspection centres. Loke also said inspection fees at all licensed centres remained standardised and regulated by the government, meaning operators could not compete on price.

items.title: Free entry to three Penang heritage sites for two days starting tomorrow in conjunction with Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites are the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum. “The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad, are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state’s heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang’s past and discover Malaysia’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Sewage turns Redang waterway black, foul-smelling
items.summary: A survey found that the sewage systems built by resort operators in the area lacked proper treatment facilities, and existing holding tanks were not considered a wastewater treatment method. Terengganu Department of Environment (DOE) director Hamzah Mohamad said the holding tanks used in the area were not a sewage treatment method, adding that every facility should have its own treatment system that complies with the prescribed standards. He said this when commenting on the sewage system at Pantai Panjang, Pulau Redang.

items.title: Federal Court hears PKR’s argument that Zuraida’s RM10m bond was reasonable; decision reserved
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Federal Court was told today that the High Court’s decision ordering former Ampang MP Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million to Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) for breaching a bond with the party was reasonable. “Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events,” he said during PKR’s appeal against a Court of Appeal decision reducing the bond payment from RM10 million to RM100,000. “The recital recorded Zuraida’s admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million.

items.title: New Lawas Hospital expected to evolve into specialist centre to cut long‑distance referrals, says deputy health minister
items.summary: LAWAS, Sept 14 — The new 76-bed Lawas Hospital is expected to evolve into a specialist hospital, thereby reducing the local population’s reliance on distant hospitals. “I hope that God willing, medical specialists will be permanently based at Lawas Hospital, rather than relying on scheduled visiting specialists. I hope this facility will become a specialist hospital,” she said at the Lawas Hospital project handover ceremony here today.

items.title: Johor's Tanjung Pelepas Port under cyberattack, launches system clean-up
items.summary: jashadiqe@nst.com.my JOHOR BARU: The Tanjung Pelepas Port (PTP), one of the world's busiest container transhipment hubs, was forced to temporarily suspend terminal operations after a cyberattack disrupted its operating systems last week. This prompted PTP to isolate the affected systems and suspend operations as a precaution while recovery efforts began. The New Straits Times contacted PTP, however, the port management declined to comment on the incident.

items.title: M & A Equity not involved in Next Lion, puts Sean Yap on administrative leave
items.summary: In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the stockbroking firm said that Sean Yap Shon Leong's involvement in Next Lion and its subsidiaries was undertaken solely in his personal capacity and not on behalf of the group. M & A Equity said Yap's involvement in Next Lion and its group of companies was not related to MAAM. The company said Next Lion and its group of companies are not subsidiaries, associated companies, joint ventures or investee companies of M & A Equity.

items.title: Abdul Aziz appointed Deputy Inspector‑General of Police
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid has been appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, effective September 9. He joined the PDRM on July 1, 1995, and has served in various departments throughout his career, including the Management Department, Special Branch, Criminal Investigation Department, Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Logistics and Technology Department, and Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department. Abdul Aziz has held several key positions, including Management Director, Deputy Director of Special Branch, Deputy Director of Narcotics, Penang Police Deputy Chief, Principal Assistant Director of Management Policy/Human Resource, and Principal Assistant Director of the Special Integrated Investigation Team.

items.title: Penang Gerakan calls for probe into alleged assault on primary student
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Gerakan has called on the Penang Education Department to investigate an alleged assault involving a 9-year-old primary school pupil. Penang Gerakan public complaints bureau chief Andrew Ooi said the complaint involved a pupil from a Chinese primary school in the southwest district who sustained bruising to his left back and arm after being hit by a teacher. He proposed regular training for teachers covering student and classroom management, anger and stress management, conflict management, child protection, appropriate disciplinary methods, mental-health awareness and counselling support.

items.title: Court of Appeal slashes Muhammad Shafee’s damages in Malaysian Bar suit to RM120,000
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages awarded to senior lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah from RM340,000 to RM120,000 in his suit against the Malaysian Bar and two others for breach of statutory duty. The bench also dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s appeal seeking an increase in the quantum of damages. On May 26, 2016, the High Court dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s suit.

items.title: Sixteen drownings in Pahang this year, Bomba urges public to respect warning signs
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 14 — A total of 16 drowning deaths have been recorded in Pahang so far this year, and the public is urged to prioritise safety when engaging in activities near rivers, waterfalls, and beaches. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations and rescue, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said key safety measures include heeding warning signs and refraining from swimming in areas identified as dangerous. “To date, 16 drowning cases resulting in 16 deaths have been recorded across the state; we advise the public to always prioritise safety and understand the risks associated with recreational areas.

items.title: Data centres must deliver more than investment: Deputy minister, MIDA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has recorded RM385.7 billion in data centre-related investments from 2021 to the first half of 2026. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Malaysia's next phase of digital infrastructure development must focus on creating economic value from the capacity being built. "The next phase is about what that capacity delivers - AI adoption, home-grown innovation, skilled talent and higher-value jobs," he said at Data Centre Nexus (DCN) 2026 today.

items.title: 3 Penang heritage sites offer free entry for two days
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill's recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites were the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum. "The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state's heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang's past and discover Malaysia's rich and diverse cultural heritage," he said in a statement today.

items.title: FGV appoints independent firm for forensic audit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) subsidiary, FGV Holdings Bhd, has appointed an independent audit firm to conduct a forensic audit regarding specific matters involving an entity with corporate ties to the group. It stressed that Felda will continue to review the need to appoint an independent audit firm to conduct a professional and comprehensive forensic audit on Felda and all organisations under the Felda Group. For the record, the forensic audit initiative against Felda has been implemented since 2019.

items.title: Toddler attack: 3 dogs yet to be caught in Johor
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Fears over stray dogs have resurfaced in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, after about 10 dogs were spotted roaming near the home of a toddler mauled last week. A resident who identified herself as Nur, 23, said authorities had caught seven dogs following the attack. Nur Haira was attacked by dogs last week and remains warded at Sultanah Aminah Hospital.

items.title: Home minister confirms police investigating Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim’s duress claim
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Police have opened an investigation paper into Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s claim that he signed an instrument of proclamation with regard to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar against his will and under duress. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said further developments would be shared if there was progress in the investigation. “The investigation paper has been opened and is still in progress.

items.title: Anthony Loke urges PH council meeting amid political uncertainty
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke will ask Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to convene a Pakatan Harapan (PH) presidential council meeting to review recent political developments amid concerns over political certainty and stability. Loke, who is also Transport Minister, said recent statements by component parties in the unity government suggested they were not moving in the same direction, potentially undermining confidence among investors and the public. I will definitely ask the Prime Minister to have a presidential council meeting in PH to review and to discuss the latest development.

items.title: Fun picnic trip turns fatal at Rompin waterfall
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said Azreen and eight friends, including five women from Felda Keratong, had gone to the waterfall for a picnic at 2pm yesterday. "They entered the water 30 minutes later. Two divers entered the water at 8.30am today and found the body 20 minutes later.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng dares Zahid, demands Penang Pakatan expel Umno and defer hikes
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has questioned why Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi dared the Pakatan Harapan-led federal government to expel Umno from Putrajaya, but did not issue the same challenge to Penang’s PH administration. Lim noted that Umno holds positions in the Penang state executive council, both city councils and state linked companies. He suggested Zahid lacked the courage to push Penang PH because the coalition would still retain a two thirds majority in the state assembly even without Umno’s two elected representatives.

items.title: GXBank gets IFC backstop for RM470mil MSME lending push
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: GXBank has secured up to US$4.95 million (RM21 million) in first-loss coverage from the International Finance Corp (IFC), which the bank calls the first risk-sharing partnership of its kind for a Malaysian digital bank. The facility aims to help GXBank expand lending to underserved micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), supporting a target loan portfolio of up to US$110 million (RM470 million). IFC will absorb initial losses on eligible loans, allowing GXBank to lend to "thin-file" businesses that lack conventional credit histories or collateral, the bank said in a statement.

items.title: Pasir Gudang API hits 152 as haze blankets parts of Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Haze blanketed parts of Johor today, with Pasir Gudang recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 152, placing it in the unhealthy category. Larkin was also in the unhealthy category, with an API reading of 150, while Pengerang recorded 114. He said the department was closely monitoring readings at all air-quality monitoring stations as several areas recorded unhealthy levels.

items.title: Petronas, PTT extends gas production from Malaysia-Thailand JDA for another 35 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) unit Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd, together with the subsidiaries of Thailand's PTT have secured a new 35-year production sharing contract (PSC) for a gas-producing block in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area (MTJDA). In a statement, Petronas said the contract for Block A-18-01 was signed by Petronas Carigali's unit PC JDA Ltd, and PTT's subsidiaries PTTEP JDX Thailand Ltd Co and PTTEP JDX Thailand (JDA) Ltd, following approvals from the Malaysian and Thai governments. Starting Jan 1, the new PSC for Block A-18-01 encompasses both the existing Block A-18 area and the additional new area, for 35 years.

items.title: Bintulu Port returns to Sarawak after 48 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port has officially returned to Sarawak's jurisdiction after 48 years under the federal government's regulatory framework. Bintulu Port was declared a federal port in 1978 and became operational in 1983. BPHB's unit Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd will continue to operate, manage and develop the port under Sarawak's regulatory framework.

items.title: Umno lacks numbers to destabilise unity government, says analyst
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno does not appear to have sufficient political strength to destabilise the unity government despite party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's challenge to the administration, an analyst said. Mazlan said Pasir Gudang member of parliament Hassan Abdul Karim had outlined the most viable options for Zahid to challenge the unity hovernment without waiting for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to expel Umno from the coalition. "First, because Umno no longer has confidence in this unity government, they can withdraw," Mazlan said when contacted.

items.title: Najib pardon delay not automatic, PAS claims objections triggered deferral
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — PAS has called on the government to explain why the Federal Territories Pardons Board deferred consideration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for a royal pardon. PAS secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter was of public interest and should not be withheld from the people. “PAS demands that the government immediately clarify this issue to the public,” he added.

items.title: Kelantan quadruplets leave home for UTHM in Johor
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Four identical brothers from Kelantan have begun their university journey together, enrolling in the same degree programme at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) today. The 23-year-old quadruplets — Amir Muttaqin, Aniq Muttaqin, Abid Muttaqin and Adib Muttaqin Md Khairuddin — were among 3,302 students registering for the 2026/2027 academic session. All four chose the Bachelor of Real Estate Management (Honours) programme at UTHM's Faculty of Technology Management and Business, having already obtained Certificates in Property Valuation from the National Institute of Valuation.

items.title: High Court acquits 15‑year‑old of Bandar Utama school murder, rules unsound mind
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 14 — The High Court today acquitted and discharged a 15-year-old boy of the charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year. Speaking to reporters outside the court, the teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident. The teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident.

items.title: Bintulu Port comes under Sarawak jurisdiction following repeal of federal Acts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Bintulu Port has officially transitioned from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government, effective September 1, 2026. Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd (BPHB) said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia that the transition follows the enactment of two acts — the Declaration of an Area in the Bintulu District to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 [Act 858] and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024 [Act 859]. It said Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd’s (BPSB) operation, management and development of Bintulu Port are governed by the heads of agreement dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak government, Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (BPA Sarawak) and BPSB, pending the execution of the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA).

items.title: Fahmi warns that communalism and corruption can weaken Malaysia’s future
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 14 — Malaysia’s younger generation must understand the country’s history and appreciate the struggles of previous generations in building a peaceful and united nation, while rejecting corruption that could undermine the country’s future. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said there were three things that could destroy a country, namely communism, communalism and corruption. He said communism had once posed a major threat to national security, with armed movements, killings and disruptions to public peace capable of undermining Malaysia’s stability.

items.title: KM263.6 southbound towards Menora Tunnel now safe for motorists after rapid slope‑erosion mitigation, says Perak exco
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 14 — The state government has assured that the North-South Expressway (PLUS) route near KM263.6, southbound towards the Meru-Ipoh Utara (Menora) Tunnel, is now safe after the area experienced slope erosion on Sept 11. Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said that authorities have carried out immediate and continuous monitoring, along with mitigation measures, to ensure traffic safety at all times. On long-term safety measures, Mohammad Nizar said PLUS is currently drafting proposals for slope structure reinforcement as well as the installation of steel netting in high-risk areas.

items.title: Fire Dept working with Public Service Dept to ensure welfare of two officers missing in Nepal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) will ensure that the welfare of its two officers who remain uncontactable following flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal last month is taken care of. Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the department had consulted the Public Service Department (PSD) on matters relating to the two officers’ salaries and pensions. He said checks showed that JBPM headquarters deputy director of the Planning and Research Division Mohd Sani Harul is due to retire on September 23, while its Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa still has many years of service remaining.

items.title: MAF ready to support emergency flying doctor service evacuations, says Chief of Defence Forces
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to deploy its air assets to assist the Health Ministry (MoH) in providing Flying Doctor Service (FDS), particularly for emergency medical evacuations in remote areas. Chief of Defence Forces Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was aimed at meeting the ministry’s urgent needs following last Tuesday’s FDS helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak. Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies, including the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), would assist the MoH in providing temporary mercy flights.

items.title: MOF tours states to gather Budget 2027 input from industries, NGOs and public, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is conducting a budget tour to gather views and suggestions from industry players, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and members of the public nationwide as it prepares for Budget 2027. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the tour aims to gain insight into the needs of key sectors in each state and obtain input from parties directly affected by government policies and allocations. Amir Hamzah said Penang is among the locations due to its important role in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI chronology: Jamil Khir among five charged since report made public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has triggered a series of investigations and legal proceedings, with a former minister becoming the latest person charged in court today. In proceedings which began at 8.45am today, former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three charges involving RM860,308,770.51 in TH funds. Apart from Jamil Khir, those charged were former TH chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, former THP Bina Sdn Bhd Security and Safety Manager Nasahruddin Ahmad, and former TH Properties Sdn Bhd deputy general manager Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, who was also a former deputy general manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan rules Sept 5 document treasonous, Tuanku Muhriz remains Yang di‑Pertuan Besar
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 14 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared that six individuals who signed a document dated September 5 seeking to depose the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan acted in a manner considered treasonous under adat and law. The Dewan said four of the signatories did not hold the positions they claimed, had issued unlawful directives to government officers, and attempted to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir without the mandatory investigation required under the state constitution. The Dewan also instructed its secretary to lodge a police report against the six individuals, noting that four of them had signed the September 5, 2026 document without holding the offices they purported to represent.

items.title: AI kiosk that can translate any language and file tourist reports? Saifuddin challenges staff to innovate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution today challenged his staff to design a kiosk operated by artificial intelligence (AI) that can translate any language and file a report with the Malaysian authorities in Bahasa Melayu. The senator described the kiosk machine as a “dream” that he wants to see materialised by his ministry as the Anwar government pushes for broad artificial intelligence adoption in day-to-day operations. “We must embrace AI and thank God we started this three years ago,” he said at the ministry’s monthly assembly here.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART team returns from Nepal humanitarian relief mission early this morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission in Nepal, arrived safely in the country at 2am today. SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent I (PgKB 1) Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the team departed from Kathmandu at 3 pm yesterday (local time) aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft, making a brief stopover in Kolkata, India, for refuelling. The SMART MAS01 team participating in the HADR mission arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on Sept 5, bringing with them 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue (SAR) equipment.

items.title: Malaysia, Thailand strengthen energy ties with new joint development area agreements, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 14 — Malaysia and Thailand today strengthened their energy partnership with the signing of a new Production Sharing Contract (PSC) and Gas Sales Agreement (GSA) for Block A-18-01 in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area (MTJDA). Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who is on a two-day working visit to Thailand, said the agreements, signed in conjunction with Gastech 2026 here, would ensure continuity in the development of the block while reinforcing investor confidence and supporting the energy security of both countries. Akmal said the progress achieved through Block A-18-01 provided a strong foundation for the continued development of the MTJDA, which represents nearly five decades of cooperation between Malaysia and Thailand.

items.title: No confidence motion? Negeri Sembilan Speaker says none filed against MB Ismail Lasim
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 14 — Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Awaludin Said today confirmed there is no motion of no confidence filed against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim for the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state assembly sitting. As reported by The Star , Awaludin said he has not received any official notice or heard of such a move following recent developments surrounding the adat issue in the state. The five-day sitting will be officially opened by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Federal govt allocates RM1.46b for eight flood mitigation projects in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 14 — The federal government, through the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), has approved eight flood mitigation projects in Melaka worth a total of RM1.46 billion for the 2021–2026 period, aiming to enhance protection for residents in flood-prone areas. He noted that the projects include the Alor Gajah Flood Mitigation Plan (RTB) Phase 1, Bandar Jasin RTB, Bandar Merlimau RTB, Sungai Putat RTB, and Sungai Duyong RTB, as well as the upgrading of the Krubong-Durian Tunggal Flood Mitigation Pond into a dual-purpose facility serving both flood mitigation and state water supply needs. “The two projects still in the pre-implementation stage are the Melaka River Flood Mitigation Project (RTB) Phase 1 and the Sungai Baru RTB in Alor Gajah; both are currently in the design phase,” he told Bernama.

items.title: Haze: 11 areas record unhealthy API readings, with Sri Aman, Serian highest at 174 at 11am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Eleven areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 11am today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings: Sri Aman and Serian (174) and Kuching (135). Overall, 55 areas recorded moderate API readings, while two areas recorded good readings.
